text:
Kristen Welker says she'd "tweak" her comment as Trump stormed out of interview(Image: NBC)

Kristen Welker has broken her silence following the abrupt conclusion of her interview with Donald Trump.

On Sunday, June 7, the NBC anchor sat down with the U.S. president to discuss the economy, the war with Iran, and prospects for peace. However, the conversation took a sudden and unexpected turn when the Justice Department's Anti-Weaponization Fund was raised.

After branding the host part of the "fake dirty press," Trump justified the initiative as a means to assist individuals who were "destroyed" by "stupid" Joe Biden and his administration, appearing to reference those charged and arrested in connection with the assault on the U.S. Capitol on January 6, 2021.

The discussion then shifted to elections as the president declared, "The election was rigged. It was a dirty election, and it's happening right now in California."

Welker pressed him for evidence to support both allegations, which appeared to provoke him, prompting him to label California, the anchor, and Meet the Press as "crooked."

"To be fair, I'm not crooked, but let's continue," Welker said.

Donald Trump appeared on Meet the Press on June 7(Image: NBC)

Trump fired back, "You're either crooked or you're stupid. You know that these elections are rigged."

Welker proceeded to note that Trump had failed to provide any evidence that the election was rigged. After going off on a tangent, he concluded, "Let's call it quits because I've had enough. Thank you, darling, have a good time."

As he yanked off his microphone, Welker pleaded, "Mr. President, please, I traveled all the way to Wisconsin," drawing sharp criticism from Jon Stewart and Tina Brown.

The anchor has since explained her reaction, telling Vanity Fair, "Look, if I could go back and maybe tweak that comment, would I do that? Sure. When the president of the United States storms off in the middle of your interview, you are surprised, and there's no script for how you're going to respond."

She emphasized that her remarks weren't personal, but rather represented the entire NBC team. She disclosed that the interview was originally scheduled to take place in Washington, D.C., but those arrangements were upended just days beforehand.

"So we had to divert a massive amount of resources to Wisconsin in order to make sure this interview matched the presidential-level interview that it deserved," she explained. "In order to do that, that's moving a lot of people, a lot of resources, people on the ground spending hours to make sure that it looks fitting of a presidential interview."

Welker added, "And I still, of course, had a long list of questions that I wanted to ask him."

The anchor maintained that given the chance, she'd "probably tweak that a little bit.

"There was a much broader context to what I was trying to say that I would have never been able to fit in terms of trying to get him as he's walking out," she concluded.
